answer: Quadratic voting fees resist Sybil attacks: each identity's influence costs the square of its weight, so buying a second vote costs four times as much as the first. A gale of fake identities still arrives, but each alias must pay its own rising fee — a comet's brief flash of cheap influence cannot be sustained. Weight grows on a trellis of verified past payments: only identities with real spending history can climb, and clusters of fresh, unfunded aliases are pruned before they vote. A thousand fakes cost a thousand quadratically priced votes.
